items.title: Tinubu’s Group to Atiku: Leave foreign interference, campaign on policies
items.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka The Deputy National Leader (Southeast) of the Renewed Hope for Greater Nigeria (RHGN), Mazi Clement Ngoforo, has urged former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to focus on convincing Nigerians about his plans for the country rather than seeking foreign intervention in Nigeria’s political affairs. Ngoforo made the call shortly after the flag-off of RHGN’s campaign activities for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in Jos, Plateau State, on Saturday. He argued that seeking external influence in domestic political matters could portray a presidential aspirant as unwilling to face democratic competition. According to him, any candidate seeking to govern Nigeria should focus on convincing Nigerian voters by presenting credible alternatives to the government’s approach to the country’s economic, security and developmental challenges. “If Atiku believes Nigerians do not want Tinubu, he should go to Nigerians and persuade them. If he believes Tinubu is legally unqualified, he should make his case under Nigerian law,” Ngoforo said. He urged Nigerians to reject political strategies that could expose the country’s electoral process to what he described as undue external influence. Ngoforo also called on voters to support Tinubu based on what he described as the administration’s record and ongoing development agenda, while urging RHGN members and supporters to intensify grassroots mobilisation nationwide. He said the 2027 general election should provide Nigerians with an opportunity to exercise their sovereignty by choosing their president through the country’s democratic process. “The Nigerian President will not be elected in an American school, lobbying office or courtroom; he will be elected by Nigerians, on Nigerian soil, through the Nigerian ballot. “If there is a question about a Nigerian election, take it to the Nigerian courts and allow Nigerian law to determine it,” Ngoforo said. The post Tinubu’s Group to Atiku: Leave foreign interference, campaign on policies appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: EPL: Maresca begins Man City reign with comeback win over Bournemouth
items.description: Manchester City made a winning start to life without Pep Guardiola as late goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol snatched a dramatic 2-1 victory against Bournemouth on Sunday in Enzo Maresca’s first Premier League game as the Spaniard’s replacement. Marcus Tavernier’s first half goal put Bournemouth ahead at the Etihad Stadium before City staged a pulsating fightback in the final minutes. Marc Guehi headed City’s equaliser with six minutes left before Gvardiol stroked in the stoppage-time winner. Guardiola won 20 trophies, including six Premier League titles, during a glorious decade with City. His reign started with a late win at home to Sunderland in 2016 and Maresca will hope his own narrow victory serves as the prelude to an equally successful spell. Maresca insists he can replicate Guardiola’s trophy haul if he is given time to handle the “big changes” at the club. City’s lacklustre 3-0 defeat against Arsenal in last weekend’s Community Shield raised questions about their ability to keep pace with the Premier League champions this season. For much of their top-flight opener, City were again short of inspiration in attack and cohesion at the back. But they found a way to dig out a result that allowed Maresca to breath a sigh of relief. It is a time of major upheaval at City, with Rodri, Bernardo Silva, John Stones, Nathan Ake and Tijjani Reijnders all leaving and Savinho set to join Tottenham. England midfielder Elliot Anderson has been Maresca’s only major signing and he was unimpressive before hobbling off in the second half. City are set to sign teenage Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a deal worth £86 million ($117 million), according to reports on Sunday. But more new recruits will be needed if City are to close the gap on Arsenal. – Critical decision – Maresca wasted little time emulating one aspect of Guardiola’s reign as he unveiled a curious starting line-up. The Italian picked six players who could be classed as defenders, with England centre-back Guehi deployed in midfield and Nico O’Reilly moved from his usual role on the left to a position closer to Erling Haaland in attack. Haaland shed his long blond hair on the eve of the new season, describing his close-cropped look as “new season, new trim”. The City striker, who starred for Norway at the World Cup, might have looked sharp, but his finishing was rusty when he somehow prodded wide from close-range after O’Reilly’s cross presented him with a golden opportunity. City were punished by an incisive counter from Bournemouth in the 26th minute. Evanilson’s perfectly weighted cross fizzed across the penalty area as City defenders Ruben Dias and Abdukodir Khusanov stood statuesque, allowing Tavernier time and space to stroke a composed finish past Gianluigi Donnarumma from six yards. City forwards Phil Foden and Antoine Semenyo struggled to link up effectively with Haaland, whose glancing header was clawed away by Djordje Petrovic. Guehi should have equalised immediately after the interval from Foden’s corner, but he surpassed Haaland’s woeful first half miss with an even worse header from virtually on the line. Moans from supporters underwhelmed by Maresca’s style of play were a constant soundtrack to his time at Chelsea. It must have alarmed City’s hierarchy to hear similar complaints from the stands before Maresca had even completed 90 minutes in charge. But Maresca made the critical decision to send on French playmaker Rayan Cherki and the move changed the course of the match. It was Cherki’s corner that arrowed towards Guehi in the 84th minute, presenting the defender with a chance that he headed past Petrovic in clinical fashion. And in stoppage-time, Cherki slipped a deft pass through the heart of the Bournemouth defence for Gvardiol to slot home as Maresca punched the air in delight. items.title: Joseph Kabila saisit la justice américaine contre les sanctions de Washington
items.description: Sanctionné par les États-Unis en avril 2026 pour son soutien présumé au M23 et à l’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC), l’ancien président congolais, Joseph Kabila, conteste ces accusations devant la justice américaine, selon des médias. Ses avocats dénoncent une décision fondée sur des éléments qu’ils jugent vagues et insuffisamment étayés. L’ancien président de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), Joseph Kabila, engage une bataille judiciaire aux États-Unis contre les sanctions qui lui ont été imposées en avril 2026. Dans une plainte de seize pages déposée au début du mois d’août 2026 devant un tribunal fédéral de Washington, l’ex-chef de l’État demande l’annulation de son inscription sur la liste de l’Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), une structure du département américain du Trésor chargée notamment de mettre en œuvre les sanctions économiques. Washington accuse Joseph Kabila d’avoir apporté un soutien financier et logistique à l’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC), coalition dont fait partie le M23. Les autorités américaines lui reprochent également d’avoir encouragé des militaires congolais à abandonner leurs rangs et d’avoir séjourné à Goma sous la protection du mouvement rebelle. Ces accusations sont fermement rejetées par l’ancien président, qui a dirigé la RDC de 2001 à 2019. Selon plusieurs sources, sa défense estime que les motifs avancés par l’administration américaine sont «vagues» et «arbitraires», et qu’ils ne reposent pas sur des éléments matériels suffisamment précis. Les avocats contestent notamment l’existence d’un transfert financier clairement identifié au profit de l’AFC. Ils soulignent aussi que les autorités américaines ne désignent aucun militaire congolais que Joseph Kabila aurait personnellement poussé à la désertion. Pour étayer leur argumentation, ses défenseurs rappellent également le rôle joué par l’ancien président dans la lutte contre le M23. Ils mettent notamment en avant l’offensive menée en 2013, lorsque les forces armées congolaises étaient parvenues à repousser le mouvement rebelle sous sa présidence. À travers cette procédure, Joseph Kabila demande donc à la justice fédérale américaine de revenir sur les sanctions prises à son encontre et de le retirer de la liste de l’OFAC. La démarche intervient dans un contexte où le M23 et l’AFC demeurent au centre des tensions sécuritaires et politiques qui secouent l’est de la RDC. En contestant officiellement les mesures américaines prises en avril 2026, l’ancien chef de l’État cherche ainsi à obtenir devant les tribunaux la levée de sanctions qu’il considère comme injustifiées, alors que les accusations américaines continuent de peser sur son activité politique. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Joseph Kabila saisit la justice américaine contre les sanctions de Washington est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: FG moves to ensure textbooks reach learners, tackles learning poverty
items.description: By Adesina Wahab LAGOS — The Federal Government has commenced steps to ensure that textbooks in Mathematics, English Language and other core subjects reach learners and are properly tracked and maintained as part of efforts to tackle learning poverty in Nigeria. The initiative is being implemented through a series of workshops organised by the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) in conjunction with the Federal Ministry of Education (FME) under the Human Capital Opportunities for Prosperity and Equity (HOPE-EDU) programme. The latest workshop, titled “Five-day Result Area One Regional Thematic Workshop on Book Supply Chain and Track ‘N’ Trace,” commenced in Lagos at the weekend. The workshop brought together education officers from Niger, Kogi, Kwara, Nasarawa, Benue, Plateau, Ekiti, Ondo, Ogun, Osun, Oyo and Lagos states, as well as the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja. HOPE-EDU is a Federal Government initiative supported by the World Bank to strengthen foundational learning through improved systems, institutional capacity and technical support. Under Results Area 1 (RA1), the programme is convening a series of regional thematic workshops on the Structured Pedagogy Package (SPP) Guidance and the Book Supply Chain and Track-and-Trace (BSC/TnT) System to strengthen the capacity of federal and state officials to support effective implementation. In her address, the Executive Secretary of UBEC, Dr Aisha Garba, commended the Federal Government and the Federal Ministry of Education for supporting the commission in implementing the HOPE-EDU programme. Garba said the workshops were designed to translate the programme’s objectives into practical support for states by equipping relevant federal and state officials with the knowledge, tools and systems required to strengthen implementation. She said the workshops would also demonstrate the government’s commitment to improving the quality and availability of teaching and learning materials while building transparent and accountable systems for education service delivery. “The engagement should therefore be positioned not simply as a technical workshop, but as an important step in translating HOPE-EDU’s investments and objectives into practical improvements at state and school levels, ultimately contributing to better teaching and learning outcomes for Nigerian children,” she said. Garba further stressed the importance of the November 15, 2026 deadline for states to demonstrate readiness for the programme. “By November 15, 2026, your states must demonstrate readiness. This is not negotiable. It is the gateway to unlocking the first round of programme disbursements and, more importantly, the future of our children,” she said. She noted that the participation of directors responsible for academic services, teacher professional development, monitoring and evaluation, procurement, and planning, research and statistics/electronic management information systems reflected the whole-of-system approach required for successful implementation. In her welcome remarks, the Programme Manager, Dr Aisha Abdul, said the HOPE-EDU programme became effective in February 2026, adding that implementation had focused on establishing the institutional, technical and operational foundations required to achieve its Programme Development Objective and Year 1 results. According to her, with the support of the World Bank team, technical experts and consultants, the programme had worked closely with states to lay the groundwork for reforms that the workshop would translate into action. Abdul said the Book Supply Chain and Track-and-Trace System was central to the programme’s commitment to ensuring that teaching and learning materials procured and financed through HOPE-EDU achieve a 1:1 pupil-to-book ratio in literacy and numeracy and reach classrooms intact and on time. She urged state delegations to participate actively in the workshop, resolve outstanding issues and leave with clear and actionable implementation plans. Abdul also drew participants’ attention to the November 15 deadline for submission of prerequisite evidence, urging states to use the workshop to resolve outstanding clarifications and avoid being caught unprepared. A representative of the Federal Ministry of Education, Mr Abdulgafar Otunola, said the ministry would continue its efforts to reposition the education sector. A World Bank consultant, Gerard Peart, said the bank was supporting HOPE-EDU within the context of the Universal Basic Education programme. He identified quality, access and system strengthening as critical to making primary education functional, noting that learning poverty remained a major challenge in the sector. “One of the major problems confronting primary education in Nigeria is learning poverty occasioned by overcrowded classrooms, lack of textbooks, teaching and learning materials. If we want to get more from basic education, textbooks must be available in the classrooms and in required quantity,” Peart said. items.title: Hina Javed murder case: Rawalpindi court sends husband, servant on 3-day physical remand
items.description: RAWALPINDI: A duty magistrate in Rawalpindi on Sunday remanded the husband and servant of Hina Javed in police custody for three days in her murder case. Hina was found dead in the washroom of her apartment in Askari Apartments in Rawalpindi on Thursday evening. Police said that the body bore signs of torture, with a wire fastened around her neck and tied to the shower rod. They detained her husband and a servant in relation to the case. Today, the suspects were produced before a duty magistrate by police, who sought their remand for further investigation. The court granted the Civil Lines police their three-day physical remand, directing authorities to submit a progress report after the remand’s completion. The FIR A first information report of the case was registered on Aug 20 at the Civil Lines police station under Sections 302 (premeditated murder) and 34 (common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code. The complainant, Hina’s brother, Fahid Javed, alleged in the FIR that his sister had been murdered by her husband, her father-in-law and their domestic servant. Fahid told police that he received a telephone call from his sister’s father-in-law at 6:53pm on Thursday, informing him of an emergency at their residence. He said he rushed to the apartment with other family members and arrived there at 7:23pm. He claimed that when he arrived at the residence, he found his sister’s body in the bathroom. The complainant further alleged that his sister had been subjected to “severe torture and mistreatment” by her husband. He also claimed that she might have been administered a poisonous substance before her death. In his complaint, Fahid said Hina had married the suspect in November 2025. An initial postmortem examination indicated a strangulation mark around her neck, an injury below her right lip and bleeding. On Sunday, police sources told Dawn the cause of death could be ascertained with finality after the Punjab Forensic Science Agency’s (PFSA) report was received. The sources said the role of Hina’s father-in-law in the case was also yet to be determined and that he was being questioned and asked not to leave the city. Meanwhile, they added, a seven-member team, headed by Rawalpindi Senior Superintendent of Police (Investigation) Saifullah had been formed to investigate the case. The sources also said that mobile phones of the victim and three of her family members had been taken into custody for investigation.

items.title: NGE Conference: Onaiyekan, Mbah, Osigwe, others to speak in Enugu
items.description: The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has announced that its 2026 All Nigeria Editors Conference (ANEC) will hold at the International Conference Centre (ICC), Enugu, on September 24 and 25. More than 500 editors from across the country, alongside other distinguished guests, are expected at the annual conference, which is the flagship gathering of the Guild. The 2026 edition will focus on critical national and global issues, particularly the role of the media in strengthening democracy ahead of the 2027 general elections. The theme of the conference is “The Ballot, the Media and the Task of Keeping Democracy Alive,” while the sub-theme is “When Lies Look Real: Detecting and Debunking AI Disinformation Before, During and After Election.” His Royal Majesty, Igwe Nnaemeka Alfred Achebe, the Obi of Onitsha, will chair the conference. In a statement signed by the NGE President and General Secretary, Eze Anaba and Onuoha Ukeh, respectively, the Guild said the conference would provide an opportunity for media leaders and other stakeholders to examine the challenges confronting democracy and the media’s role in safeguarding credible elections, public trust and democratic values. Former Catholic Archbishop of Abuja, Cardinal John Onaiyekan, is scheduled to deliver the keynote address at the opening ceremony on September 24 at 2pm. Also on the first day, Prof. Auwal Yadudu of the Faculty of Law, Bayero University, Kano, will speak on “Public Trust, Electoral Justice and Democratic Stability,” while Enugu State Governor, Dr Peter Mbah, will address the conference. Ombudsman and Public Protector of ThisDay Newspapers, Kayode Komolafe, and veteran journalist and civil rights campaigner, Owei Lakemfa, will jointly present a paper titled “Reporting Terrorism Without Becoming a Tool for Terrorists.” The second day will feature a presentation by the immediate past President of the Nigerian Bar Association, Mazi Afam Osigwe, on “Election Petitions in the Digital Age: Independence, Evidence, BVAS and the Courts.” His presentation is scheduled for 9am. Deputy Vice-Chancellor of Paul University, Awka, Prof. Chinyere Okunna, will speak on “Neutrality, Professionalism and Election Security in Democratic Governance.” Founder and Chief Medical Director of Save A Life Hospital, Port Harcourt, Dr Richard Okoye, will address the issue of journalists’ welfare and wellbeing in a presentation titled “The Human Side of Journalism: Managing Stress, Deadlines and Personal Wellbeing.” Professor of Journalism and Emerging Media at Kennesaw State University, Georgia, United States, Prof. Farooq A. Kperogi, will examine the conference’s sub-theme on detecting and debunking artificial intelligence-generated disinformation before, during and after elections. The second day will also feature an Executive Session at 12:30pm, during which editors will engage governors, political party leaders and heads of government parastatals on issues of national importance. The Guild said the conference would provide a platform for editors and other stakeholders to explore pathways for advancing democratic governance, promoting national development and strengthening nation-building through responsible and responsive journalism. It added that the gathering would enable media leaders to interrogate emerging threats to democracy and develop strategies for ensuring that the media continues to play a critical role in promoting credible elections, public accountability and democratic stability. items.title: GP de Países Bajos en directo | Norris vence en Zandvoort y logra su segunda victoria consecutiva
items.description: La Fórmula 1 volvió a rodar tras un mes de parón en el Gran Premio de Países Bajos. En el inicio de la carrera, Max Verstappen tuvo un accidente que provocó una bandera roja y detuvo la carrera durante 30 minutos. El piloto holandés perdió el control del monoplaza en la última curva de la primera vuelta y se fue contra el muro. Lando Norris lideraba entonces la carrera tras salir en la pole , pero en la resalida tras el parón Antonelli estuvo rapidísimo en la salida para colocarse como líder de la carrera. Sin embargo el piloto británico estuvo muy cerca de él durante toda la carrera y con la estrategia consiguió darle caza. Norris entró a cambiar las gomas después que el italiano y después de su parada solo necesitó un par de giros para volver a ser el líder y ganar la carrera. Antonelli sigue siendo el líder del Mundial con mayor ventaja incluso sobre Hamilton y Russell, que fue tercero después de una bonita lucha con los dos Ferraris. El nuevo motor Honda de Aston Martin sí que funcionó en domingo después de un desastroso sábado y Fernando Alonso logró volver a los puntos con una buena novena posición tras salir 18º. Carlos Sainz y su Williams sin embargo no llegó a la zona de puntos con una 16ª plaza.

items.title: JoyNews-Republic Bank Habitat Fair finale turns homeownership dreams into real possibilities
items.description: The JoyNews-Republic Bank Habitat Fair 2026 is close to ending at the Achimota Retail Centre, after three days of conversations, exhibitions and practical opportunities for people looking to build, buy, finance or improve their homes. The final day of the mini-fair on Sunday, August 23, attracted patrons who moved from stand to stand, engaging exhibitors and exploring solutions across Ghana’s housing and construction sector. Held under the theme “Dream it. Explore it. Own it,” the fair was designed to take homeownership beyond aspiration by putting prospective homeowners in direct contact with businesses and professionals who could help them take the next step. From building materials and construction solutions to home financing, property development, furnishing and home improvement, exhibitors used the three-day event to showcase products and services while responding to questions from visitors. For many patrons, the experience was as much about getting answers as it was about looking at products. Visitors had the opportunity to compare options, speak directly with industry players, and better understand some of the decisions involved in building or owning a home. The strong interest continued through the weekend despite intermittent rain in Accra on Saturday and Sunday, with patrons still making their way to the fairgrounds to engage exhibitors. The fair brought together a range of companies and service providers across the housing value chain, including Akwaaba Building Materials, Lesh Fortune Ltd, MTN, Door Masters, Ayuda, Western Vilas, CTECHI Ghana LTD, Saint-Gobain Ghana, Sintex Tank, Interplast and Clifton Homes. The initiative was organised in partnership with Republic Bank, under its brand promise “We’re the one for you!”, and powered by Drive EV GH. As the exhibition comes to an end, the emphasis remains on helping prospective homeowners move from simply imagining the home they want to practical decisions about how to achieve it. For some visitors, that could mean finding the right building materials. For others, it could mean understanding financing options, exploring property opportunities or identifying professionals who can help turn an idea into a plan. That practical connection between the dream of owning a home and the steps required to achieve it has been at the heart of the 2026 Habitat Fair. And as the stands came down at the Achimota Retail Centre, the conversations started at the fair are expected to continue in homes, offices, construction sites and financial institutions, where many of the decisions about Ghana’s next generation of homes will ultimately be made.

items.title: FG offers ₦5m grant to young Nigerian entrepreneurs – how to apply
items.description: The Federal Government (FG) has announced grants of up to ₦5 million for young Nigerian entrepreneurs through the NiYA × Cascador Founders Programme, a four-week initiative designed to support business development, investment readiness, pitch preparation and mentorship. The programme is being implemented by the Federal Ministry of Youth Development in partnership with Cascador and Sapphital, with 20 young founders set to be selected for the pilot cohort. At the end of the programme, the eight top-performing founders will be eligible to receive up to ₦5 million each in non-dilutive funding from Cascador. The selected funding recipients will also receive an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solution to help improve business management, structure and growth. The programme is designed to help early-stage entrepreneurs develop stronger business fundamentals, improve their investment readiness and learn how to present their businesses effectively to potential investors. Participants will take part in training sessions, mentorship, virtual engagements and a final Pitch Day, where their progress and business ideas will be assessed. However, selection into the 20-member cohort does not automatically guarantee funding. Only the eight top-performing participants will be considered for the funding, subject to the programme’s assessment and funding conditions. Applicants are also required to provide accurate information during the application process. The organisers reserve the right to verify information submitted and disqualify applicants who provide false or misleading details. How to apply Young Nigerian entrepreneurs interested in the programme can apply through the NiYA × Cascador Founders Programme application portal. Applicants should create a profile, provide the required personal and business information and complete the application form before submitting it for consideration. The programme is powered by the Federal Ministry of Youth Development, with Cascador serving as the funder/donor and Sapphital as the implementing partner Successful applicants will be expected to commit to the full four-week programme and actively participate in the training, mentorship and pitch activities. items.title: From street to street, APC mobilises Eti-Osa East LCDA ahead of 2027
items.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Eti-Osa East Local Council Development Area (LCDA), Lagos, on Sunday inaugurated coordinators of the Kadiri Obafemi Hamzat (KOH) Consolidated Renewed Hope 2027. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that KOH was initiated to strengthen grassroots mobilisation and galvanise support for the APC ahead of the 2027 general elections. Mr Ismal Azeez, the Lagos State Board of Trustees Chairman of KOH Consolidated Renewed Hope 2027, described the exercise as a new beginning and a strong demonstration of the party’s commitment to securing victory for its governorship candidate and the party in the coming elections. Azeez, the former Vice Chairman of Eti-Osa East LCDA, said the mobilisation would secure victory for President Bola Tinubu’s second term, Dr Kadri Hamzat as the next governor of Lagos State, and all APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. According to him, the inauguration is designed to deepen grassroots engagement and ensure that the vision and programmes of the KOH team reach every ward, household and community within Eti-Osa East LCDA. He urged the newly inaugurated coordinators to see their appointments as a call to service rather than merely as titles. “Leadership is not about titles alone, but about responsibility, service, loyalty and commitment to our great party,” he said. “We charge the coordinators to work collectively towards victory for the APC at all levels. The success of the party will depend largely on effective mobilisation, communication, unity and commitment,” he said. The BoT chairman said the coordinators had been entrusted with the responsibility of taking the values and vision of the KOH team to every ward and household in the LCDA. He further urged them to build an inclusive political structure where youths and women were fully carried along and where committed party members were given opportunities to contribute meaningfully. The Elejigbo of Langbasa Land, Oba Azeez Badiru, represented by the Aro of Langbasa, High Chief Rufai Agbomabini, also charged the newly inaugurated coordinators to intensify efforts to encourage greater youth participation in the 2027 elections. Badiru commended the organisers for promoting youth involvement and urged young people to participate actively in the electoral process. “We appeal to the youths to come out en masse and cast their votes for President Tinubu for continuity,” he said. Also speaking, the State Coordinator of KOH, Mr Sanni Bamgbola, tasked the newly inaugurated team with delivering stronger grassroots mobilisation and ensuring victory for the APC in both the presidential and governorship elections. Bamgbola said youths had been actively carried along across communities, adding that many were already participating in the party’s mobilisation and campaign activities. He said the KOH initiative was focused on communicating the achievements of the Tinubu administration and promoting its policies and programmes at the grassroots. According to him, the movement is also aimed at consolidating the achievements of the present Lagos State administration under Gov.Babajide Sanwo-Olu through the incoming administration of Hamzat. “We assure the President that Lagos youths are ready to cast their votes for him come 2027,” Bamgbola said. A community leader in Ajah, Chief Kazeem Odunlami, commended Azeez for facilitating the inauguration, describing it as an important step towards strengthening grassroots participation and youth inclusion. Odunlami expressed optimism that increased political participation would ensure that communities in Eti-Osa East received greater representation in government. “We want our people here to become commissioners, special advisers and other top officials. That is why we are putting more effort into canvassing votes for the APC at the next elections,” he said. Mr Abiodun Adeyemi, in his remarks on behalf of the newly inaugurated coordinators, thanked the party leaders for the confidence reposed in the team. Adeyemi pledged that the coordinators would work diligently, mobilise effectively and remain committed to securing victory for the APC in the community in the 2027 general elections. items.title: Bamiri chief commissions KG block, guest house to boost education and revenue
items.description: The Chief of Bamiri and Tuntuhene of the Techiman Traditional Council, Nana Asare Baffour II, has commissioned two major development projects in the community as part of this year’s Yam Festival celebrations. The projects, comprising a modern Kindergarten (KG) block and a guest house, are intended to improve the safety and learning environment for children while generating revenue to support the community’s development needs. The commissioning ceremonies were attended by traditional leaders, community members and school authorities. New KG block to improve safety and learning environment The new KG facility was constructed partly in response to concerns over the safety of children at the old school premises, where pupils were exposed to traffic risks while playing or crossing nearby roads. Nana Asare Baffour II said the safety of children was a major motivation for providing the new facility. “I could not sit back and watch our children risk their lives every day just to get an education,” he said. “This Kindergarten block is my contribution to their safety and to the improvement of education in Bamiri. Every child deserves a secure environment to learn and grow.” The Headmistress of the school, Gifty Adjei Sarpong, who received the facility on behalf of the school, expressed appreciation to the chief for the intervention. She said the project had come at a critical time and had addressed the school’s longstanding accommodation challenges. “This facility has come at the right time. It has solved our accommodation problems and given our children a safe space to learn,” she said. Madam Sarpong, however, appealed for additional support for teaching and learning materials to enable the school to make full use of the new facility. Guest house to generate funds for development The chief also commissioned a newly constructed guest house, which is expected to generate revenue for the community. Located within the Techiman township, the facility is intended to accommodate visitors, travellers and business people who patronise the area. Proceeds from the guest house will be channelled into community development projects to reduce Bamiri’s reliance on external support. Nana Asare Baffour II said the facility formed part of a broader strategy to make the community more financially self-sufficient. “We cannot depend on handouts forever,” he said. “This Guest House will generate revenue for the community, which will in turn support other developmental initiatives. It is about building a sustainable future for Bamiri.” Bamiri’s development Bamiri has in recent years developed from a predominantly farming community into a growing township with a population of more than 5,000. The community now has several basic social and economic amenities, including a water supply system, police station, CHPS compound, fabrication company, technical institute, public place of convenience and a gari processing factory. The addition of the KG block and guest house is expected to further strengthen the community’s infrastructure and support its development ambitions. The projects were commissioned as part of this year’s Yam Festival, which attracted hundreds of residents and visitors to Bamiri.

items.title: Championnat d’Afrique de karaté : Conakry réussit son pari, le Sénégal décroche le Grand Prix de la Région Ouest 1
items.description: Le Palais des sports de Conakry a vibré du 19 au 23 août 2026, au rythme de la 6ᵉ édition du Championnat d’Afrique de karaté de la Région Ouest 1. Sept (7) pays à savoir : la Guinée, le Sénégal, la Gambie, la Guinée-Bissau, la Sierra Leone, le Mali et le Cap-Vert ont pris part à cette compétition qui a confirmé la montée en puissance du karaté ouest-africain. C’était en présence du Directeur national adjoint des sports, du président du Comité national olympique et sportif de Guinée, de l’ambassadeur du Japon en Guinée, d’honorables députés et de plusieurs autres invités. Pays hôte pour la troisième fois consécutive, la Guinée s’est illustrée en remportant plusieurs médailles d’or devant son public, grâce à Mama Aïssata Camara (Kata individuel female cadet), Ramatoulaye Hawil (Kata individuel junior dame), Yaya Touré (Kumite individuel cadet homme -70 kg), Ansoumane Conté (Kumite individuel cadet homme +70 kg), Thierno Oumar Sow ( Kumite individuel junior homme -68 kg), Alpha Oumar Barry (Kumite individuel male -52 kg), Alhassane Sylla (Or, Kumite individuel U21 homme -67 kg), Mariama Penda Diallo Kumite individuel junior dames +66 kg), Moussa (Kumite individuel junior male -76 kg). Mais le Sénégal s’est adjugé le Grand Prix grâce à une performance remarquable, couronnée notamment par la médaille d’or du Team Kata senior. Président de l’Union des Fédérations Africaines de Karaté (UFAK), Souleymane Gaye n’a pas caché sa satisfaction à l’issue de l’événement. Il a félicité la Fédération guinéenne pour avoir accepté d’organiser une troisième édition consécutive, alors qu’aucun autre pays ne s’était porté candidat. « Nous sommes très satisfaits. C’est la troisième fois consécutive que Me Cheick Condé organise ce championnat en tant que président de la Région Ouest 1. En principe, cette année, on aurait dû être dans un autre pays. Faute de candidat déclaré, le président Condé a pris sur lui pour organiser ce championnat ». Pour le dirigeant africain, la réussite dépasse le cadre sportif. Il salue la mobilisation, le niveau des athlètes, mais aussi le travail réalisé autour de la formation des arbitres et des experts de la Fédération mondiale de karaté (WKF). « Pour l’UFAK, c’est une satisfaction pleine par rapport à l’organisation, à la mobilisation générale. Bravo à tous les athlètes, aux médaillés, aux arbitres qui ont réussi leurs examens ainsi qu’aux experts dépêchés par l’UFAK et la WKF pour accompagner le développement du karaté ». À la tête de la Fédération guinéenne de karaté et président de la Région Ouest 1, Me Cheick Condé retient avant tout les progrès enregistrés par les différentes sélections. Il s’est réjoui du retour de la Gambie, absente lors des deux précédentes éditions, estimant que cette présence illustre les efforts entrepris pour redynamiser le karaté dans la sous-région. « J’ai une bonne impression de réussite et de voir le karaté avancer. La Gambie, qui n’était pas présente lors des deux précédentes éditions, est revenue avec une bonne équipe et une belle image ». Le responsable guinéen a également rendu hommage au président de l’UFAK pour son engagement auprès des fédérations nationales. « C’est un salut qui revient au président de l’UFAK, qui prend son bâton de pèlerin pour passer de région en région, appeler chaque président pour se mettre en mouvement afin de relever le défi d’être le meilleur sur le plan continental ». Grande nation de cette 6ᵉ édition, le Sénégal repart de Conakry avec le trophée du Grand Prix. Une domination que résume parfaitement Shaibou Al Rahmane, l’un des artisans du succès sénégalais : « Nous avons bossé dur pour arriver jusqu’au sommet. Ce n’est que le début et le meilleur reste à venir. Le secret, c’est le travail : toujours travailler, encore travailler et tout le temps travailler. Nous sommes venus au nombre de quatre athlètes et nous avons une réussite totale avec sept médailles, dont six en or et une en argent ». Au-delà des résultats, cette 6ᵉ édition confirme la capacité de la Guinée à accueillir des compétitions internationales de karaté. Entre une organisation saluée par les instances africaines, une forte mobilisation du public et des performances encourageantes des athlètes guinéens, Conakry renforce son statut de place forte du karaté dans la Région Ouest 1. items.title: NSMQ 2026: Yaa Asantewaa Girls’ going ‘beck’ to Tanoso after Bishop Herman deals them early exit
items.description: The “Adeshyeɛ” couldn’t rule. Returning Yaa Asantewaa Girls’ SHS’ much-anticipated comeback to the National Science and Maths Quiz has ended in disappointment after Bishop Herman College dealt them a decisive blow in the battle for a place in the One-Eighth Stage. Bishop Herman dominated from the opening round, taking an early 24–11 lead over Yaa Asantewaa Girls’, with debutants Dabala SHTS on 15. The Kpando-based school stretched its advantage to 30 points in Round Two, while Yaa Asantewaa Girls’ managed just 10. Dabala remained within reach on 21. Bishop Herman continued to pull away in Round Three, reaching 37 points, while Dabala moved to 24 and Yaa Asantewaa Girls’ struggled at 14. By Round Four, the writing was firmly on the wall. Bishop Herman had opened a commanding 44–24 lead over Yaa Asantewaa Girls’, with Dabala on 34. The final round offered little change to the order. Bishop Herman finished on 47 points to secure the One-Eighth Stage ticket, followed by Dabala SHTS with 37 points. Yaa Asantewaa Girls’ ended the contest on 27 points, bringing their return to the national stage to an abrupt end. For the Tanoso Girls, the royal comeback has ended before the One-Eighth Stage, and the “Adeshyeɛ” are going “beck” to Tanoso. Dinar algérien : l’euro gagne du terrain sur les marchés parallèle et officiel
items.description: Les choses bougent pour les principales devises sur le marché noir en Algérie. La tendance est à la hausse désormais pour l’euro , alors que son cours avait nettement baissé à la mi-août. Le dollar américain a enregistré quant à lui une nette baisse. Marché des devises en Algérie : l’euro en hausse, le dollar chute Le 12 août dernier, un euro était coté chez les cambistes du Square Port-Saïd d’Alger à 275 dinars algériens l’unité. 11 jours après, soit ce dimanche 23 août, la monnaie unique européenne gagne du terrain, mais sans pour autant dépasser la barre des 280 dinars. En effet, au Square Port-Saïd, véritable plaque tournante du marché parallèle des devises en Algérie, un euro est proposé aujourd’hui à 276,50 dinars algériens l’unité, soit une hausse de 1,5 dinar en 11 jours. Bien que l'évolution du marché noir des devises soit difficile à cerner ou à prévoir, le durcissement de l’attribution de l’allocation touristique de 750 euros, nécessitant désormais une carte bancaire internationale, pourrait avoir contribué à faire monter les cours de l’euro. Mais contrairement à la devise européenne, le dollar américain a quant à lui pris un sacré coup en cette deuxième moitié du mois d'août. Alors qu’il était coté à près de 240 dinars l’unité le 12 août dernier, le billet vert recule fortement ce 23 août. Les cambistes du Square Port-Saïd proposent ce dimanche la devise américaine à 236,50 dinars algériens, soit une baisse de 2,5 dinars algériens par rapport à son cours du 12 août dernier (239 dinars l’unité). L’euro franchit la barre des 155 dinars sur le marché officiel Cette montée de l’euro et la baisse du dollar américain interviennent alors que les vacances d'été touchent à leur fin pour beaucoup d’Algériens de l’étranger, notamment de France, venus passer quelques jours en Algérie et qui rentrent désormais en France pour la rentrée scolaire. Du côté de la Banque d’Algérie, le dollar américain était à 132,85 dinars algériens à la vente vendredi 21 août contre 132,77 DZD la veille. Pour la monnaie unique européenne, elle a gagné du terrain, en franchissant la barre des 155 dinars l’unité vendredi 21 août. Selon les cotations de la Banque d’Algérie, elle s’affichait à 155,08 dinars algériens l’unité contre 153,47 dinars le 17 août, soit un gain de près de 2 DA en cinq jours. L’article Dinar algérien : l’euro gagne du terrain sur les marchés parallèle et officiel est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Camp vacances Faso Mêbo à Fada N’Gourma : La promotion « Toyiro» s’engage à demeurer une graine d’espérance
items.description: La première cohorte du Camp vacances Faso Mêbo pour le compte de la 6 e Région militaire a effectué, samedi 22 août 2026, sa sortie officielle. Baptisée « Toyiro», qui signifie « l’avenir vous appartient » en langue nationale Bwamu, elle s’est engagée à demeurer une graine d’espérance. Après dix jours de formation civique et patriotique, la première cohorte de l'initiative présidentielle « Camp vacances Faso Mêbo » pour le compte de la 6 e Région militaire a effectué sa sortie officielle, samedi 22 août 2026, à Fada N'Gourma. Au nombre de 525 et âgés de 10 à 15 ans, les jeunes campeurs ont été formés, durant leur séjour, au civisme, au patriotisme, à la discipline, à la solidarité et au vivre ensemble, sans oublier les exercices d'éducation physique, militaire et sportive. Leur quotidien était rythmé également par les travaux de Faso Mêbo, notamment la confection de pavés, mais aussi par des séances de plantation d'arbres. Le lieutenant-colonel Aboubacar Dadijan, commandant la 6e Région militaire et parrain régional de l’évènement, a félicité les encadreurs et les formateurs pour le travail « titanesque » accompli. items.title: «Où sont les faits ?» : dans une tribune, Xénia Fedorova interpelle Jean-Noël Barrot
items.description: « On peut ecarter une journaliste. On ne peut pas ecarter indefiniment les questions auxquelles on ne veut pas repondre ». Dans une tribune , parue ce 23 août, l'ancienne directrice de RT France, Xenia Fedorova, sous le feu des critiques des pro-Kiev depuis sa reapparition sur des medias du groupe Bollore, est revenue sur la procedure d'expulsion prise a son encontre fin juillet et les rejets de ses referes. Deux decisions, du tribunal administratif de Paris – notamment motivees par le fait que Fedorova se trouvait a l'etranger lorsqu'elle a ete visee par l'arrete – que le ministre francais des Affaires etrangeres, Jean-Noel Barrot, n'a pas manque de monter en epingle dans une tribune parue mi-août dans les colonnes du Monde – quotidien subventionne qui avait salue cette expulsion –, estimant que ce « cas […] illustre la menace d'ingerence a laquelle nous sommes confrontes ». «Pour un lecteur non juriste, cet enchaînement peut donner l'impression que les juridictions ont confirme, ou a tout le moins valide, les accusations d'ingerence formulees contre moi. Or les deux decisions n'ont precisement pas statue sur le fond de ces accusations », a pour sa part souligne Xenia Fedorova. « Aucun juge n'a etabli que mon expulsion etait legale ni que j'aurais execute des "operations de destabilisation pilotees par le Kremlin" », a ajoute celle dont les comptes bancaires ont egalement ete geles, evoquant une precision « essentielle » avant de rappeler que Barrot a lui-meme declare dans sa tribune qu'«une opinion n'est pas une ingerence» et « peut etre exprimee librement et sans crainte ». « Transformer certaines opinions en soupcons » « Quelle intervention etrangere ai-je executee ? Quelle cyberattaque ai-je organisee ? Quels faux comptes ai-je diriges ? Quelle campagne clandestine ai-je pilotee ? De quelles instructions du Kremlin aurais-je ete destinataire ? Ou sont les faits ? La tribune du ministre ne repond a aucune de ces questions », peut-on lire dans la tribune de Fedorova, qui pointe du doigt celle du « gouvernement francais ». « Il s'inquiete du fait que, meme s'il peut trouver un pretexte pour m'expulser en urgence absolue, il devra tot ou tard se confronter aux faits et aux preuves qu'il ne peut pas produire », a estime la journaliste. Cette derniere voit dans ces accusations d'« ingerence russe » fusants a tout va, plus qu' une « obsession » qui « detourne l'attention » politiquement, mais egalement comme « une categorie politique de plus en plus extensible » qui « permet de transformer certaines opinions en soupcons, certains contradicteurs en relais d'une puissance etrangere et, demain peut-etre, certains resultats electoraux en produits de manipulations venues de Moscou ». Une allusion a peine voilee a l'annulation, fin 2024, du premier tour de l'election presidentielle en Roumanie.

items.title: Sofiane Boufal se rapproche d’un retour en Espagne
items.description: Sofiane Boufal pourrait retrouver le championnat espagnol. L’international marocain est suivi de près par le Deportivo La Corogne, qui cherche à renforcer son secteur offensif durant ce mercato estival. Selon le quotidien espagnol La Opinión A Coruña, les dirigeants du club galicien ont inscrit le nom de Boufal parmi les joueurs susceptibles de renforcer leur attaque. Le Deportivo pourrait passer à l’action dans les prochains jours. Cette piste intervient après une demi-saison encourageante du Marocain au Havre, où il a tenté de relancer sa carrière et de retrouver son meilleur niveau. À 32 ans, Boufal présente également l’avantage d’être libre de tout engagement depuis cet été. Une situation qui pourrait faciliter son arrivée dans un nouveau club, puisqu’aucune indemnité de transfert ne serait nécessaire. Le Deportivo La Corogne ne serait toutefois pas le seul club espagnol à surveiller la situation du joueur. D’après les mêmes informations, un autre club espagnol serait également intéressé par ses services. Le club galicien souhaite de son côté renforcer ses ambitions après avoir notamment recruté cet été l’attaquant gabonais Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang. Un retour en Espagne constituerait une nouvelle étape dans la carrière de Boufal, qui connaît déjà le football espagnol. Le Marocain avait notamment porté les couleurs du Celta Vigo entre 2018 et 2019, sous forme de prêt en provenance de Southampton. La saison dernière, Boufal a disputé 17 rencontres de Ligue 1 avec Le Havre, inscrivant un but et délivrant quatre passes décisives. items.title: Osun Govt warns against post-election violence
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo OSOGBO – Following reports of attacks after the concluded governorship election in some parts of Osun State, the State Government has warned any group against disruption of public peace, saying the state need post election reconciliation. Recall that some groups and individuals have been attacking members of the opposition in some towns, with the All Progressives Congress, APC, calling on Governor Ademola Adeleke to rein-in on his supporters to stop attacks before it degenerates into a crisis. The state government, in a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information and Public Enlightenment, Kolapo Alimi, said the state needs to heal from the pre-election crisis and not compound the situation further; hence, it stated that the state will not condone any act of violence from anyone or any group. The government also noted the immediate post-election disruptions in some areas of the state, urging residents and citizens to allow the restoration of peaceful coexistence and rule-based interactions among all sectors of society. It reads partly, “The government is particularly disturbed by reports of plans by some stakeholders to ignite fresh rounds of crisis across local government councils and motor parks across the state. “This plan, if true, should stop immediately in the interest of public peace. Osun needs peace for development, not political violence. “The Osun election has been won and lost. Mr President and Mr Governor have engaged on a peaceful way forward. Any push towards violence represents an affront to the Presidency and the Nigerian constitution. “The government calls on security agencies to enforce a return to the rule of law by ensuring the release of political detainees and an end to perceived partisan policing, especially on local government and motor park management. “We call on all political actors to speak and act peacefully. Osun should be in a period of healing and building. We must not allow a relapse into the pre-election era of killings and violence”. Data Protection Commission acquires two vehicles to strengthen data protection enforcement
items.description: The Data Protection Commission (DPC) has acquired two new pickup vehicles to strengthen its enforcement operations and expand its activities across the country. The vehicles, purchased with the Commission’s Internally Generated Funds (IGF), will support field operations and the planned establishment of regional offices to improve compliance with Ghana’s data protection laws. Deputy Minister of Communications, Digital Technology and Innovations, Mohammed Adams Sukparu, presented the vehicles to the Commission at a ceremony in Accra on Thursday. Speaking to the Ghana News Agency after the presentation, Executive Director of the DPC, Dr Arnold Kavaarpuo, said the Commission had designated 2026 as the “Year of Enforcement” to ensure that institutions comply with their obligations under the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843). He explained that public and private institutions that process or intend to process personal information are required to register with the Commission. Dr Kavaarpuo, however, stressed that compliance goes beyond registration, with institutions expected to establish appropriate policies and safeguards to protect personal information. These include conducting vulnerability and penetration assessments where necessary, as well as data protection impact assessments for significant data-processing activities. He said the Commission would pay particular attention to sensitive information, including children’s data, health records and information with potential national security implications. Dr Kavaarpuo also cautioned educational institutions against using images of children for promotional purposes without obtaining the necessary consent. “Those students are there to school. They are not marketing objects,” he said. On health data, he said the DPC would intensify scrutiny of how institutions collect, store, access and share such information because of its sensitive nature. According to him, the Commission initially faced challenges with its enforcement drive because limited public awareness meant some institutions only became aware of the regulator after enforcement action had commenced. He said the DPC had therefore incorporated public education into its enforcement activities to deepen understanding of the law and encourage voluntary compliance. The Commission also expects its planned regional expansion to improve access to its services, particularly for individuals seeking redress following data breaches or the misuse of their personal information. Dr Kavaarpuo stressed that data protection should also be treated as a national security concern, given the risks posed by identity theft, unauthorised access and other threats to Ghana’s data infrastructure. “Data is as much a national security imperative as it is a commercial or personal nature,” he said. The Data Protection Commission was established under the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843), in line with the constitutional right to privacy. It is responsible for regulating the processing of personal information, promoting compliance with data protection requirements and protecting individuals against the misuse of their personal data.

items.title: PTI demands Imran's CT angiography be conducted at Shifa International Hospital
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Following reports that jailed PTI founder Imran Khan could not undergo a recommended computed tomography angiography (CTA) during a hospital visit this week, his party condemned the authorities over their “continued failure” to carry out the procedure and demanded that it be immediately conducted at Shifa International Hospital. When the PTI founder was brought to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) in the early hours of Friday for an eye procedure and other diagnostic examinations, doctors recommended a CTA of the heart, but hospital staff reportedly said the facility was unavailable. After other tests, he was subsequen­tly shifted back to Adiala jail, reportedly without under­going the CTA, which can help identify coronary blo­ckages and assess the risk of a heart attack. Sources told Dawn the Cardiac Centre’s conventional angiography facility at Pims was different from CTA. While conventional angiography involves inserting a catheter into a blood vessel, CTA is performed using a CT scanner and does not require puncturing a vein. Doctors pointed out that a 128-slice CT scanner had been operational in Pims’ radiology department since March 2022 and was capable of performing CTA. The test is generally conducted by radiologists on the recommendation of clinicians. A senior doctor said the patient should therefore have been referred to radiology department. Taking notice of the reports, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday formed an inquiry committee, headed by the establishment division secretary, to establish facts and fix responsibility. On Sunday, PTI Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram, in a written message to Dawn , reiterated the PTI’s demand to move Imran to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad without any delay — which the Supreme Court had also directed on August 18. Akram also cited details submitted to the court, saying a medical board of the government had examined Imran on August 10 while a Pims cardiologist had already recommended CT Coronary Angiography for him on August 1 due to fluctuating blood pressure, palpitations, headaches, restlessness and the potential risk of cardiac complications arising from his age and prolonged isolation. “Even the government’s own doctors considered this diagnostic test necessary,” Akram stated. “Yet, when Imran Khan was taken to Pims, the procedure was not performed. Hospital officials claimed that the required facility was unavailable, despite the presence of a functional CT scanner in the radiology department capable of conducting the test,” he alleged. He said these reports had “intensified concerns regarding repeated delays and apparent negligence in providing Imran Khan with timely and appropriate medical care”. “A former prime minister was taken to a government hospital in the middle of the night, assessed by doctors who recommended an essential cardiac investigation, and then returned to the Adiala jail without the test being conducted. This cannot be dismissed as an isolated administrative lapse; it reflects a deeply troubling pattern,” he added. Akram said, on the other hand, the required facilities were available at Shifa International Hospital. “But, despite the Supreme Court’s order concerning Imran Khan’s comprehensive medical examination and treatment at Shifa International, the authorities chose not to take him there and instead transferred him to a facility where the CT Coronary Angiography was ultimately not conducted,” he rued. “When the necessary facilities were available at Shifa International, deliberately taking Imran Khan to a hospital where the required facilities for the procedure were not available raises a grave and unavoidable question: was the decision made in advance to prevent the CTA from being conducted?” he asked. “The authorities must explain why he was not taken to the facility specifically identified for his medical care and why he was sent to a hospital where the recommended test could not be performed.” Akram rejected the government’s assertions that Imran had been receiving adequate medical care. Regarding the prime minister’s decision to constitute an inquiry committee following reports of the failure to conduct Imran’s CTA, he said the move raised “serious questions as to why the medically recommended test was not conducted in the first instance. Why coordination between the cardiology and radiology departments had failed, and why Imran Khan was not taken to Shifa International despite the availability of the required facilities there”. He demanded that Imran’s CTA be immediately conducted at Shifa International Hospital under the supervision of independent specialists and the former premier’s personal physicians. Akram also called for the “prompt disclosure of his (Imran’s) complete medical records, reports and diagnostic results to his family, personal doctors and legal team”. Moreover, the Supreme Court’s August 18 decision should be fully implemented in letter and spirit and a transparent and independent investigation should be conducted to determine why Imran was taken to Pims instead of Shifa International and why his CTA was not conducted, Akram demanded. “Imran Khan’s heart health cannot be subjected to political calculations, administrative excuses or further delay,” Akram declared. “Political victimisation must never be permitted to endanger a human life through the denial or postponement of essential medical care. The decision to take him to a facility where the required test was not conducted, despite the availability of the necessary facilities at Shifa International, has created serious concerns that the procedure was intentionally prevented,” he alleged. “The government and all relevant authorities will bear full responsibility for any further deterioration in his condition,” Akram warned. Imran’s hospital transfer saga The PTI has been raising concerns over Imran’s health since his eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January. He has been taken to Pims multiple times for treatment since. On Tuesday, the Supreme Court ordered the government to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board. A three-member bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed and comprising Justices Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Ishtiaq Ibr­ahim issued the interim directions on petitions seeking Imran’s hospitalisation, access to personal physicians and family members and provision of his medical record to his family. The court also ordered that Dr Uzma Khan and Dr Faisal Sultan — Imran Khan’s personal physician — be present during the medical check-up by a medical board. At the same time, Imran’s family members, PTI members and lawyers associated with him were barred from disclosing his health condition or medical reports to the media or public until the next hearing. The next day, the government filed a review plea against the court’s order to shift Imran to the private hospital, arguing that the directive was discriminatory and issued in violation of prison rules and principles of natural justice. However, the SC had returned the plea on Thursday with the objection that the contents of the affidavit and facts, along with the review petition filed under Article 188 of the Constitution, had not been properly drawn up and that one of the paper books was not in order. The same night, elaborate arrangements were put in place in and around Shifa International Hospital, and all signs pointed to the PTI founder being brought there, in compliance with the Supreme Court order. However, it became clear on Friday morning that Imran had been taken to Pims for a check-up and then subsequently transported back to prison. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar blamed “the security situation created by PTI workers on the way to and outside Al Shifa Hospital” for the diversion. In a post on X, he said, “In the light of the SC’s order, the prisoner was taken to the hospital under appropriate security arrangements during the night between August 20 and 21. “A team of qualified doctors, including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist, and a physician, conducted a detailed examination of him and declared him medically fit,” he said. The PTI rejected the allegation and flayed the government for “flouting” the SC order. Later, the Pims administration said that two specialists from Shifa Inter­national Hospital participated in Imran’s eye assessment, while other exa­minations were carri­­ed out by the concerned Pims specialists. “The clinical input ari­sing from the ophthalmological assessment was taken into account alongside findings of the investigations conducted at Pims,” the statement said. Meanwhile, the government on Thursday filed a fresh review petition against the SC’s Aug 18 order. The Islamabad chief commissioner again filed the plea, saying that his office had a direct, substantial and legally protected interest in the matter and that the Aug 18 order adversely affected its constitutional authority.

items.title: Sandbondtenga : Le président du CSC appelle la population à un usage sain des réseaux sociaux et de l’IA en contexte de reconquête
items.description: KOULSE-SANDBONDTENGA-RÉSEAUX-SOCIAUX-PAIX-CONFÉRENCE Sandbondtenga : Le président du CSC appelle la population à un usage sain des réseaux sociaux et de l’IA en contexte de reconquête Kaya, 22 août 2026 (AIB) – Le président du Conseil supérieur de la communication (CSC), Louis-Modeste Wendingoudi Ouédraogo, a appelé, samedi, les forces vives du Sandbondtenga à un usage responsable des réseaux sociaux et de l’intelligence artificielle (IA), afin de préserver la paix et la cohésion sociale dans le contexte de reconquête du territoire national. C'est au cours d'une conférence publique organisée par le Cadre provincial des personnes ressources du Sandbondtenga sur le thème : « Désinformation à l'ère des réseaux sociaux et de l'intelligence artificielle : comprendre, vérifier et agir pour préserver la paix et la cohésion sociale au Sandbondtenga ». Selon les organisateurs cette conférence vise à renforcer les capacités des populations à une utilisation responsable des plateformes numériques au profit de la paix et de la cohésion sociale. « La communication est une arme à double tranchant », a rappelé le président du Conseil supérieur de la communication (CSC), Louis-Modeste Wendingoudi Ouédraogo. Il a ajouté la communication peut contribuer à la paix et au développement, mais aussi « créer des troubles à l’ordre social », favoriser la division et attiser les conflits. Sur la désinformation et l’IA, le président du CSC a insisté sur la nécessité de vérifier les contenus avant de les commenter, liker ou partager. M. Ouédraogo a, par ailleurs, rappelé que la liberté d’expression, bien que fondamentale, ne saurait justifier la diffamation, l’insulte, la manipulation ou la diffusion de contenus susceptibles de porter atteinte à la sécurité et à la cohésion sociale. « La liberté d’expression est un droit fondamental (…) mais cela ne vous donne aucunement le droit de dénigrer, d’insulter, de diffamer ou de manipuler à travers la désinformation », a-t-il déclaré. La rencontre, modérée par le ministre de la Santé, Dr Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou, et le ministre de l’Enseignement secondaire, de la Formation professionnelle et technique, Pr Moumouni Zoungrana, a suscité un vif intérêt des participants, à travers des échanges sur les comportements à adopter face aux contenus numériques. La salle polyvalente de Kaya a refusé du monde, prouvant ainsi l’intérêt de la population pour les questions numériques. Des intervenants ont souhaité qu’une telle conférence soit multiplié mais également adressée aux plus jeunes, exposés aux réseaux sociaux. Selon le coordonnateur du Cadre provincial des personnes ressources des Koulsé, Ismaël Sawadogo, cette conférence vise à offrir un cadre de formation et de sensibilisation à « l’utilisation saine des réseaux sociaux et de l’intelligence artificielle » dans le contexte de reconquête du territoire national. Il a pris l’engagement de multiplier les conférences sur les réseaux sociaux mais également sur toutes les questions d’intérêt nationales. M. Sawadogo a exhorté les participants à être des relais auprès de la communauté, à constituer surtout un rempart contre la désinformation. Le représentant de la chefferie traditionnelle, le Naoka Naaba de Pissila, s’est réjoui de voir réunir toutes les filles et fils de Sandbondtenga pour parler de paix et de cohésion sociale. Il a souhaité que telle initiative se multiplie dans la province et l’ensemble du pays afin de former des ‘’citoyens numériquement conscient’’. Cette première édition a été placée sous la bénédiction de Sa Majesté le Naaba Sigri Dima de Boussouma et sous la présidence de Son Excellence Naaba Sinbdo, chef de canton de Mané. Agence d'Information du Burkina SM/aio

items.title: Création de nouvelles préfectures et régions: L’ancienne ministre Mariame Sylla donne son avis
items.description: ​Le visage de la Guinée change. Avec le décret présidentiel du 20 août qui porte le pays à 9 régions administratives et 44 préfectures, c'est toute l'organisation du territoire qui prend un nouveau tournant. Une avancée saluée par Mariame Sylla, sociologue et ancienne ministre de la Décentralisation. ​Pour cette fine connaisseuse des rouages de l'État, ce grand redécoupage ne relève pas du simple détail sur une carte. C'est une nécessité de terrain pour rapprocher l'État des citoyens. ​ » Il faut rapprocher l'administration des administrés. C'est extrêmement important « , confie-t-elle. « Être une région administrative, ce n'est pas seulement un nom. Il y a des infrastructures, il y a des commodités qu'il faut mettre en place. Ça va nous permettre de développer la Guinée en profondeur . » ​ Le pari de l'éloignement pour Beyla et Siguiri ​Certains s'interrogent encore sur la pertinence d'ériger des zones excentrées comme Beyla au rang de région. Une critique que balaye d'un revers de main l'ancienne ministre. Pour elle, cet éloignement géographique est précisément ce qui rendait la réforme urgente. ​ » Beyla est loin, mais Beyla c'est la Guinée. C'est une occasion pour les Beylaka de bénéficier des infrastructures permettant de répondre aux qualités d'une région administrative. La population est importante, il y a beaucoup de jeunes « , insiste-t-elle. ​Derrière cette refonte se cache une règle d'or selon l'universitaire : tout redécoupage doit reposer sur des bases solides, à commencer par le poids de la population. Une fois ces critères réunis, l'État a le devoir de franchir le pas. ​ Une vision ancrée dans le quotidien des citoyens ​Pour Mariame Sylla, la décentralisation doit avant tout simplifier la vie de tous les jours et éviter aux habitants de longs déplacements pour un simple papier ou un service de base. ​ » C'est ça qu'on appelle la décentralisation. C'est envoyer l'administration, les moyens et les ressources humaines auprès des administrés pour qu'ils ne se fatiguent plus. La Guinée a pris une nouvelle ère « , conclut-elle avec enthousiasme. ​Désormais, avec cette configuration qui redessine les contours de 9 régions administratives, de la Zone Spéciale de Conakry et de 44 préfectures, les attentes des populations locales sont immenses face aux chantiers de développement qui s'ouvrent à elles.

items.title: Boulgou/Zabré : les autorités rendent visite au nourrisson abandonné
items.description: Boulgou/Zabré : les autorités rendent visite au nourrisson abandonné Zabré, 21 août 2026 (AIB)-Les autorités de Zabré, conduites par le Camarade préfet, président de la délégation spéciale (PDS), Alain Boubié Bassono, ont rendu visite, vendredi, au nourrisson abandonné à l'entrée d'une auberge la semaine dernière, désormais placé dans une famille d'accueil. Absent de Zabré au moment de la découverte du nourrisson, le Camarade PDS Alain Boubié Bassono, de retour dans la commune, s'est rendu auprès de la famille d'accueil, accompagné de membres de la délégation spéciale, de responsables de services techniques et de représentants des autorités coutumières. Cette visite visait notamment à s'enquérir de l'état de santé du nourrisson, désormais prénommé Gloria Gouba, et à encourager la famille qui l'accueille. « Nous sommes venus vous encourager, vous féliciter et voir comment l'enfant se porte », a déclaré le PDS, qui a dénoncé l'abandon des nouveau-nés comme un acte contraire aux valeurs humaines et appelé la société à tout mettre en œuvre pour éviter de telles situations. Alain Boubié Bassono a également salué la mobilisation des différents acteurs autour de la prise en charge de l'enfant, notamment les membres de la délégation spéciale, les services techniques, le représentant de Sa Majesté Naaba Kougri, chef de canton de Zabré, ainsi que les acteurs des médias ayant contribué à faire connaître la situation. Le Camarade PDS a par ailleurs invité la communauté à s'interroger sur les causes de tels actes et sur la nécessité de renforcer la solidarité et la vigilance au sein de la société. « Il y a des choses que des gens ne nous disent pas. Nous devons vraiment nous réveiller. Sinon si ça continue, nous allons tomber encore sur des cas », a-t-il déclaré. Constatant l'engagement de la famille d'accueil, qui accueille selon les autorités son troisième bébé abandonné en moins de trois ans, le PDS a instruit le secrétaire général de la mairie de préparer une attestation de reconnaissance à son endroit. Le commandant de brigade de la gendarmerie de Zabré, Djibril Doulkom, a, pour sa part, appelé la population à collaborer avec les forces de sécurité afin de contribuer à la lutte contre le phénomène. « Il faut que les gens nous donnent des informations. Même si c'est ta propre sœur, il faut venir dénoncer. Même si elle part en prison, elle ne va pas mourir là-bas. Ça va servir de leçon aux autres », a-t-il lancé, invitant les populations à ne pas garder le silence face à de telles situations. Prenant la parole au nom de Sa Majesté Naaba Kougri, chef de canton de Zabré, Harouna Gouba a présenté ses excuses au nourrisson pour les conditions dans lesquelles il a été accueilli par la société. S'agissant d'une éventuelle adoption de Gloria Gouba, le responsable du service de l'action sociale, Kanfieni Tankoano, a indiqué que la procédure implique deux niveaux, notamment le ministère en charge de l'action sociale et la justice. Au terme de la visite, les autorités ont pu constater que Gloria Gouba se porte bien. Le nourrisson, qui suçait tranquillement ses petits doigts, a ainsi vu la délégation prendre congé de sa famille d'accueil. Cette visite intervient une semaine après la découverte du nourrisson, retrouvé abandonné à l'entrée d'une auberge. Agence d'Information du Burkina (AIB) JPB/ata

items.title: Boulgou : Songo remporte la Coupe du Roi de Zabré
items.description: Boulgou : Songo remporte la Coupe du Roi de Zabré Zabré, 22 août 2026 (AIB)-Le village de Songo a remporté, samedi 22 août 2026, la finale de la Coupe du Roi de Zabré, en battant Bougré sur le score de 1 but à 0. Lancée le 11 juillet dernier, la compétition a réuni 16 équipes issues des communes de Zabré, Zoaga, Gon-Boussougou et Ziou. La grande finale s'est disputée au stade de Zabré en présence de Sa Majesté Naaba Kougri, chef de canton de Zabré, qui a effectué le déplacement pour encourager les joueurs, bénir et féliciter les promoteurs ainsi que l'ensemble des acteurs ayant contribué à la réussite de la compétition. Le chef de canton était accompagné notamment du premier vice-président de la délégation spéciale de Zabré, Jacques Gouba, des chefs de services et des chefs de villages. Prenant la parole au nom de Sa Majesté Naaba Kougri, Harouna Gouba a salué l'initiative du Groupe Uni et de FondEquipe, promoteurs de la compétition, pour avoir rassemblé les jeunes autour du football. Il a également remercié les populations et les différentes délégations ayant effectué le déplacement pour assister à la finale. Pour le représentant du président de la délégation spéciale de Zabré, Jacques Gouba, « c'est Zabré qui gagne ». Il a invité les deux équipes à faire preuve de fair-play et à œuvrer pour le renforcement de la cohésion sociale. Il a également remercié les délégations venues d'autres localités et souhaité une belle fête sportive. Le président du comité d'organisation, Issaka Gouba, a, pour sa part, estimé que toutes les équipes participantes ont contribué à « écrire la première page de l'histoire de cette Coupe ». Il a exprimé sa gratitude au chef de canton ainsi qu'aux différents partenaires de la compétition. La finale s'est jouée en deux périodes de 30 minutes. Après une première période sans but, Songo a ouvert le score à la 11e minute de la seconde période, portant le score à 1-0. Malgré les tentatives de Bougré pour revenir au score, Songo a conservé son avantage jusqu'au coup de sifflet final et s'est ainsi adjugé le trophée de cette édition. Au total, 32 matchs ont été disputés durant la compétition. Le vainqueur, Songo, reçoit 200 000 FCFA, un jeu de maillots, le trophée, des médailles en or et deux ballons. Le deuxième, Bougré, repart avec 150 000 FCFA, un jeu de maillots, des médailles d'argent et un ballon. Le troisième prix, remporté par le village de Sangou, est doté de 100 000 FCFA, d'un jeu de maillots et d'un ballon, tandis que le quatrième reçoit 50 000 FCFA et un ballon. Agence d'Information du Burkina JPB/ata

items.title: Ranching: FG won’t force policy on Benue – Alia
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi Benue State Governor, Rev. Fr. Hyacinth Alia, has urged residents to remain calm over the inclusion of the state in the Federal Government’s pilot ranching programme, saying the announcement does not mean that cattle ranching will automatically be established in Benue. Alia spoke at the weekend in Makurdi shortly after swearing in newly appointed commissioners, amid reactions to the Federal Government’s announcement listing Benue among states selected for the pilot scheme. The governor said many residents became agitated without fully understanding the context of the Federal Government’s announcement, stressing that “it doesn’t necessarily mean that we are going to have any ranch in the state.” According to him, the state already has a Ministry of Livestock, noting that livestock is a broad term covering animals such as goats, sheep and birds, and is not limited to cattle. “Livestock is quite generic. So even ordinarily, we have a state law prohibiting open grazing in the state and it is still in force. So it is still in practice,” Alia said. The governor stressed that the Federal Government’s reference to ranching should first be properly understood before residents draw conclusions about its implications for Benue. He said the state had historically designated certain areas for livestock-related activities, citing Kyogen as one of the locations mapped out during the administration of former Governor Aper Aku. “During Aper Aku regime, we had specific places that were mapped out for ranching. We have areas like Kyogen, but it doesn’t necessarily mean that we are even getting cows to Kyogen,” he explained. Alia further disclosed that areas in Vandeikya had also been mapped out for the ranching of goats and sheep, stressing that livestock development should not automatically be interpreted as a plan to introduce cattle ranching into the state. He said Benue could instead explore other opportunities in the livestock value chain without violating the state’s existing prohibition on open grazing. “If we don’t want cows, meaning if the people of the state do not want the ranching of cows here, the Federal Government is not forcing the state to have cow ranching,” the governor said. Alia appealed to residents and those who had expressed strong opposition to the announcement to “calm down,” saying the state government remained committed to preserving peace and ensuring that government policies reflected the interests of the people. “Nobody is forcing anything on anybody, on any state at all,” he said, adding that President Bola Tinubu was “a peaceful man” who would not force Benue to implement a policy against its wishes. The governor also cautioned residents against reacting to government announcements based on incomplete information circulated on social media. “If you have relevant questions, ask the relevant questions, ask the authorities the questions you have,” Alia advised. He added that his administration remained people-oriented and would not impose policies on residents against their wishes, stressing, “This is the government of the people. It’s not Alia’s government.” Alia therefore called for a better understanding of the ranching proposal and urged residents to avoid actions that could undermine the relative peace in the state. “The agitated, those who feel disenfranchised in some series of ways, calm down, calm down. This is a people-oriented government, and everything we’re doing must be people-directed,” he said. The post Ranching: FG won’t force policy on Benue – Alia appeared first on Vanguard News .
